newsitem.title: USA: Raines-US economy strong, can absorb spending cuts.
newsitem.headline: Raines-US economy strong, can absorb spending cuts.

text.p: White House Office of Management and Budget Director Franklin Raines said Friday that it was a good time to balance the budget because the U.S. economy is strong and can absorb spending cuts.

"The time to balance the budget is now," Raines said in testimony prepared for a Senate Budget Committee hearing. "Our economy is strong, so it can absorb the spending cuts that we would have to put in place."
Raines said President Clinton and Congress have voiced their commitment to reach a budget agreement this year.
"So I am cautiously optimistic. But I am realistic as well," he said.
To avoid past pitfalls when agreements have not worked out, "we have to work together, in good faith," he said, adding that Clinton and his administration were prepared to do that.
Raines said Clinton's budget is credible to accomplish deficit reduction.
"We are proposing a credible budget to finish the job," he said.
Raines said Clinton's budget has "real savings, based on conservative assumptions," and is grounded in conservative economic and technical assumptions.
"With pleasant surprises such as the recent fourth quarter GDP figures, we expect that, if anything, the economy will continue to outperform our projections," he said.
Clinton's budget shrinks federal spending to an estimated 19 percent of GDP in 2002 from 22.5 percent in 1992, Raines said.
